concerns.text: T015 requires extracting 3D trajectories from 2D video frames using 'OpenCV + YOLOv8' to compare against PyBullet ground truth. The spec (FR-002) and plan do not define a method for recovering 3D depth/position from single-view 2D video without depth sensors or multi-view geometry. This task silently relaxes the physical validity constraint by proposing a technically impossible or highly unreliable heuristic (2D-to-3D lifting) as a substitute for the required 'trajectory continuity' metric, violating the physics-consistency verification principle.

T037b mandates fetching real-world data from RobotBench and raising a 'RuntimeError' if missing. The spec (FR-008) and plan explicitly state that validation can use 'MuJoCo or real-world data' (an OR condition). By making real-world data a hard dependency that blocks execution if missing, the task narrows the acceptance criteria and violates the spec's flexibility, potentially causing the entire evaluation phase to fail even if the MuJoCo ground truth path is viable.

T007b and T016 hardcode a 'discard_rate: 0.4' (40%). The spec (FR-003, SC-001) and plan explicitly mark the discard rate as '[deferred]' to be determined by the research design or pilot. While the plan notes a 40% target, the spec's use of '[deferred]' indicates the value is not yet a fixed requirement. Hardcoding this value in the tasks without a mechanism to override it or a note that this is a provisional placeholder constitutes a silent narrowing of the experimental parameter space, violating the requirement to keep the value deferred until the research design is finalized.

T013 explicitly selects 'Wan-Turbo (distilled 100M)' from HuggingFace. The spec (FR-001) and plan refer generally to 'Wan2.1' and mention 'Wan-Turbo' as a potential option but do not mandate the specific '100M' variant. Locking in a specific model variant that may not exist or match the 'Wan2.1' architecture described in the spec risks a scope drift where the implementation uses a different model than the one specified, violating the requirement to use the specified Wan2.1 model family.
